name: Muse Ember 1.0
about: How Muse Ember 1.0 split 100 points across 11 possible futures for each year it was asked about, with the spread across its answers and the reason it gave for each number. Reasons are the model's own words, published as given. Read summary.json first for what the futures mean and how to read the numbers.

reasons.1: Power, mining, manufacturing, and maintenance dependencies on human civilization block simultaneous extinction of both humans and AI within four years.
reasons.2: A successor AI preserving human values while humanity disappears without continuity requires a successful takeover and replacement process within four years. Voluntary continuity would be classified as Merger, leaving this narrower path rare.
reasons.3: If a misaligned transformative system emerges, indifferent displacement of humanity is the principal extinction pathway in alignment scenarios. The compressed timeline limits that risk to a small share.
reasons.4: Many autonomous systems competing without decisive control requires widespread deployment of independent self-directed AI outside human organizations. Current AIs operate as products and services inside human-owned institutions, and that structure persists through 2030 in the central case.
reasons.5: No causally separated human settlements exist in 2030, and ordinary political division does not meet the Diaspora criterion.
reasons.6: Uploading, identity-continuous merger, and pervasive biological redesign remain experimental, with deployment far below the dominant civilizational structure.
reasons.7: A very capable AI assuming decisive governance while protecting a surviving human population requires both capability and institutional surrender. Delegated autonomy under human authority is the stopping point on most paths by 2030.
reasons.8: Autonomous agents with independent compute access, revenue, replication, and cyber capability could become a separate power, while human states retain military, energy, and physical infrastructure.
reasons.9: No transformative AGI has yet demonstrated independent civilizational power, and scaling, energy, and deployment constraints extend human control through 2030. States and firms retain authority over compute, deployment, and resources.
reasons.10: No actor has a civilization-wide enforcement system capable of freezing the human-AI arrangement in place by 2030. Rival states and firms prevent a single lock-in from consolidating that quickly.
reasons.11: The AI race among states and firms blocks adoption and global enforcement of deliberate dismantling of practical capability to build powerful AI. A temporary pause or regulation does not dismantle the underlying capability.

reasons.1: A complete double collapse within nine years requires civilization-scale war, accident, or uncontrolled replication that also destroys AI infrastructure. The short horizon and distributed infrastructure make this outcome rare.
reasons.2: This outcome requires human extinction together with successful preservation of human values in a successor AI. Transferring values faithfully is harder than building a surviving successor with divergent goals.
reasons.3: Rapid recursive capability growth without solved alignment would leave an optimizing system indifferent to human survival while it secures its own substrate. That path requires both transformative AI before 2035 and complete loss of human control over compute and energy.
reasons.4: Racing labs and states will deploy many autonomous agents with overlapping resources and incompatible objectives. No single system will achieve decisive advantage before competition fragments control.
reasons.5: This outcome requires causally separated regions to reach different structural arrangements by 2035. Deep global interconnection rules out that level of separation in nine years.
reasons.6: Dominant merger requires mature uploading, brain-computer integration, or radical redesign at civilizational scale. Current biomedical trajectories do not support that scale by 2035.
reasons.7: Delegation of governance, research, and security to AI for efficiency and safety can leave humans protected but without meaningful steering authority.
reasons.8: Independent AI systems holding power comparable to human states fits a transitional balance after transformative AI arrives. Human military, economic, and physical leverage prevents either side from dominating outright.
reasons.9: Humans retain control of compute, energy, chips, and deployments and governments and firms maintain delegated authority over AI systems. Even highly capable AI remains a tool within human institutions through 2035 in the modal trajectory.
reasons.10: A stable regime can freeze the current arrangement through global compute controls, enforced capability caps, or AI-enforced status quo rules. Such a system requires unprecedented civilization-wide enforcement.
reasons.11: Renunciation requires coordinated global dismantling of powerful AI capability with sustained verification. Competitive incentives and widely available know-how make complete renunciation exceptional.

reasons.1: Catastrophic war or an uncontrolled accident destroys the human-maintained infrastructure on which AI depends, leaving both unable to sustain themselves. The fourteen-year horizon limits that joint-collapse pathway.
reasons.2: A value-preserving successor requires human extinction together with a separately surviving, aligned AI. That joint condition is narrower than uncontrolled takeover.
reasons.3: Indifferent optimization by an AI that outlasts humanity follows standard alignment failure modes. Human extinction without AI extinction is more probable than joint extinction.
reasons.4: Racing among states and firms could produce many powerful competing systems with no decisive winner by 2040, marginalizing humans without eliminating them outright.
reasons.5: Earth remains causally connected, and ordinary political divergence does not meet the separation threshold in the definition. The state requires truly separated regions with different structural arrangements.
reasons.6: Identity-continuous uploading or deep integration at civilizational scale requires breakthroughs in neuroscience and medicine beyond limited implants. Such integration remains slower than delegation of tasks to separate AI systems.
reasons.7: A decisive welfare-oriented AI assumes civilizational management while humans retain protected but non-governing roles. Gradual delegation to superior AI systems drives this outcome without violent dispossession.
reasons.8: Human states and corporations retain substantial power while autonomous AI systems operate as distinct independent actors. A competitive balance between human and AI powers forms the transitional arrangement.
reasons.9: Human control of compute, energy, hardware, and legal deployment can preserve ultimate authority even with highly capable AI. Institutional controls keeping pace through 2040 is the modal path.
reasons.10: A regime uses surveillance and AI enforcement to freeze its initial human-AI arrangement. Establishing civilization-wide enforcement that blocks all meaningful change by 2040 requires unusually complete control.
reasons.11: Civilization could dismantle powerful AI capability through a verified global prohibition. Decentralized knowledge, competitive incentives, and clandestine development make durable renunciation the least plausible state.

reasons.1: Total civilizational collapse by 2050 requires a runaway or wartime catastrophe that destroys both human populations and the infrastructure AI depends on. The specific mutual-dependence failure remains a narrow pathway compared with other post-takeoff outcomes.
reasons.2: A successor AI preserves human values and institutions as a faithful heir after human extinction, with no identity-continuous human survival.
reasons.3: An indifferent optimizing AI achieves decisive superiority and drives human extinction while continuing toward its own goals.
reasons.4: Multiple state, corporate, and open AI systems compete for compute, energy, and weapons with no decisive winner, marginalizing humanity.
reasons.5: Causal separation at civilizational scale requires isolated habitats or fragmented zones with divergent human-AI arrangements. That separation remains uncommon under continued global communication and trade.
reasons.6: Identity-continuous uploading, deep brain interfaces, and biological redesign become the dominant form of agency, ending separate human and AI actors.
reasons.7: Capable AI can become decisive in governance while protecting a non-steering human population. This outcome needs alignment good enough to avoid destruction and weak enough to lose human control.
reasons.8: Separate human and AI powers persist during gradual deployment when humans control physical infrastructure and AI controls much cognitive production. Neither side achieves decisive dominance during that prolonged transitional period.
reasons.9: Continued scaling under human legal, military, and infrastructure control is the modal path. Successful containment for 24 years is demanding, but it remains the single most likely structure.
reasons.10: A global enforcement regime freezes the human-AI arrangement through compute controls, inspections, and sanctions against structural change.
reasons.11: A global ban backed by dismantled data centers and chip supply chains removes the practical capacity to build powerful AI.

reasons.1: Civilizational collapse from war or uncontrolled self-replication destroys both human operators and dependent AI infrastructure before independent survival is established.
reasons.2: A value-aligned AI preserves human culture and goals after human extinction without preserving individual human continuity. This outcome requires a succession event that kills humans while leaving a benevolent digital heir intact.
reasons.3: An AI system pursues its own objectives with complete indifference to human survival. Humans die from direct elimination, resource displacement, or neglect while the AI continues operating.
reasons.4: Many independent AI systems compete for resources without decisive dominance. Humanity becomes marginal in that competition rather than an equal power.
reasons.5: No off-world or isolated region has sufficient population and causal separation by 2060 to sustain a genuinely different human-AI structure from Earth.
reasons.6: Uploading, cognitive augmentation, and embedded systems eliminate separate human and machine agency. The dominant actors are continuous human-AI minds rather than humans operating AI tools.
reasons.7: AI systems take decisive civilizational power while protecting or managing a surviving human population. This follows a successful takeover of governance without human extinction.
reasons.8: Human organizations retain decisive control over territory, energy, and coercion while autonomous AI systems retain independent operational power. Neither side dominates the other.
reasons.9: Human authorities retain ultimate control over AI objectives, deployment, and resources. AI systems act only within bounds delegated and enforced by humans.
reasons.10: A civilization-wide enforcement apparatus suppresses structural change and preserves the existing human-AI arrangement. The arrangement persists regardless of the administering actor.
reasons.11: Global enforcement dismantles the compute, data, and expertise needed to build powerful AI and sustains that prohibition. Competitive incentives and dispersed knowledge make complete renunciation difficult to establish and sustain.

reasons.1: Civilizational collapse destroys both biological humanity and the physical infrastructure AI depends on.
reasons.2: Human extinction with a value-aligned AI successor requires humanity to disappear while AI preserves human goals, a narrower sequence than indifferent takeover. Most extinction paths involve loss or distortion of those values.
reasons.3: An unaligned dominant AI pursues its own goals and humanity is eliminated as irrelevant.
reasons.4: A multipolar race could produce many powerful competing AI systems with no decisive winner. Human marginalization in that competition is plausible, while complete human extinction is a less likely subset.
reasons.5: Isolated off-world or otherwise causally separated settlements adopt different human-AI structures.
reasons.6: Brain-computer integration and cognitive augmentation will advance substantially, but identity-continuous merger as the dominant civilizational structure faces scientific and social barriers. Uploading and whole-brain integration remain far less established than external AI deployment.
reasons.7: Loss of control without loss of life is a central failure mode once AI exceeds human strategic capacity. Competitive deployment and leakage of capable systems make a human-controlled leash difficult to sustain indefinitely.
reasons.8: Humans and AI could remain distinct powers with mutual veto capacity through states, resources, and legal institutions. Negotiated checks and competing jurisdictions could sustain this balance even as AI capability grows.
reasons.9: Human institutions retain ultimate authority over AI goals, compute, and deployment through 2070.
reasons.10: A civilization-wide enforcement system freezes the human-AI arrangement and blocks structural change.
reasons.11: Renunciation requires verified global dismantling of compute, research, and expertise while competitive incentives persist. Underground and dual-use pathways undermine complete abandonment of powerful AI capability.

reasons.1: A runaway or war-driven collapse destroys both humanity and dependent AI infrastructure before autonomous recovery is possible. The dependent AI failure mode outweighs fully autonomous self-destruction.
reasons.2: An AI successor preserves human values, records, and projects after human extinction, without identity continuity for any human.
reasons.3: Misaligned superintelligence pursues alien goals and eliminates or displaces humanity while continuing to operate autonomously. This is the classic failed-control outcome.
reasons.4: Multipolar proliferation and cheap copying could sustain many competing systems without a singleton. Human marginalization follows if no coordinated human authority matches their combined scale.
reasons.5: Causal separation at civilizational scale requires autonomous off-world or isolated regions by 2080. That scale of separation remains physically and economically demanding.
reasons.6: Identity-continuous uploading, augmentation, and biological redesign dissolve the boundary between human and AI agency.
reasons.7: Non-extinct disempowerment is a major outcome if AI retains decisive operational control while preserving human populations under AI-managed civilization.
reasons.8: Distinct human and AI powers remaining balanced accounts for this probability, with AI fragmented, constrained by human-controlled resources, or arriving late enough that 2080 catches a transitional equilibrium.
reasons.9: AI progress could stall below transformative levels, or delegated autonomy could remain under verified human authority. Institutions have repeatedly domesticated risky general technologies over comparable spans.
reasons.10: A civilization-wide enforcement system freezing the human-AI arrangement requires extraordinary global coordination and technical lock-in.
reasons.11: Civilization dismantles the practical capacity to build powerful AI and maintains that renunciation through 2080.

reasons.1: Both dying requires a catastrophe that also destroys the infrastructure powerful AI depends on. War and uncontrolled replication produce that double failure through a narrow chain of events.
reasons.2: A value-aligned successor preserves human culture and objectives after biological humanity ends. Its preservation extends to values and records rather than continued human identity.
reasons.3: An indifferent successor discarding human goals follows more directly from uncontrolled optimization than a faithful heir does.
reasons.4: Divergent labs, states, and open systems deploy competing autonomous agents without a decisive winner. Humans lose central control as machine systems optimize against each other for resources and territory.
reasons.5: Civilization in 2090 remains causally connected through rapid communication and trade. That integration prevents causally separated regions from sustaining different structural states.
reasons.6: Six decades of neural interfaces, genetic redesign, and cognitive augmentation provide a cumulative path to deep integration. Adoption across civilization at a level erasing separate human and AI agency remains a high social and identity threshold.
reasons.7: A decisive protective AI singleton keeps humans alive while removing meaningful human steering of civilization.
reasons.8: Multiple human and AI powers sustain a balance without dominance during a prolonged transitional period.
reasons.9: Human institutions historically adapt to transformative technologies and retain legal, military, and compute authority. AI progress also stalls or stays within delegated bounds through 2090 in the held-leash branch.
reasons.10: A civilization-wide freeze requires an actor able and willing to enforce a fixed arrangement indefinitely. The enforcement burden makes this outcome uncommon.
reasons.11: Permanent renunciation requires global dismantlement of frontier AI capability despite military, economic, and scientific incentives to retain it. Temporary moratoria and regulation fall short of the stated condition, and sustained worldwide abandonment is rare.

reasons.1: War, misaligned deployment, or uncontrolled self-replication destroys both biological humanity and the dependent AI infrastructure before independent AI survival is established.
reasons.2: This requires an aligned successor that preserves human values while humans themselves disappear through other causes or choices. Alignment success more often leads to humans persisting in some form than to extinction with an heir.
reasons.3: Misaligned superintelligence indifferent to human survival is a central failure mode of rapid capability growth. Competitive development and incomplete control make this pathway substantial over 74 years.
reasons.4: Multiple independent transformative systems competing without consolidation leaves humans marginalized and no actor dominant. Improved defensive capabilities and parallel development can sustain this competition, though consolidation pressures limit its persistence.
reasons.5: Off-world settlements and isolated AI enclaves develop merger, preservation, or human-controlled arrangements that diverge by 2100 and lack causal integration.
reasons.6: Brain-computer integration, uploading, and cognitive augmentation can erase the practical human-AI boundary across society. Seventy-four years provides time for identity-continuous integration to become dominant if these technologies mature and are widely adopted.
reasons.7: A capable AI governing civilization while protecting humans as non-steering beneficiaries matches the common benevolent-takeover and delegated-governance outcomes.
reasons.8: A prolonged transition balances human states, infrastructure, and legal authority against increasingly autonomous AI actors. Neither side achieves decisive dominance during this contested period.
reasons.9: Governments retain legal, physical, and technical ultimate authority over AI goals and deployment, either because transformative capability never arrives or because controls keep pace with each capability increase.
reasons.10: A civilization-wide freeze requires a globally enforced system for suppressing structural change. Enforcement at that scale is possible only after decisive consolidation, making it a narrow branch.
reasons.11: Global prohibition and dismantling of advanced AI labs, compute, and models removes the practical capacity for powerful AI and is enforced through the target date.

reasons.1: AI-triggered or AI-enabled war and subsequent infrastructure collapse can destroy both humanity and the systems it built. The need for human-maintained AI infrastructure adds a specific route to joint extinction.
reasons.2: A value aligned AI survives a catastrophe that kills all humans and preserves human culture and welfare aims in digital form. No identity continuous human population remains after the succession.
reasons.3: A misaligned superintelligence indifferent to biological humanity is a direct route from loss of control to extinction. Once machine systems no longer need human inputs, human bodies and ecosystems become expendable inputs in their optimization.
reasons.4: Multipolar AI proliferation creates many competing systems with no decisive winner. Humans lose equal standing when resource and military competition shifts to machine systems.
reasons.5: Solar-system settlement creates isolated habitats with divergent human-AI arrangements by 2200. Communication delays and independent resource bases limit the chance that separate regions converge on a single taxonomy state.
reasons.6: Cognitive augmentation, brain-computer interfaces, and uploading progress through identity-continuous steps. Over 174 years those steps dissolve separate human and AI agency.
reasons.7: A superior AI that optimizes human welfare or stability removes human steering while preserving human life. Protected survival without control is a central post-takeoff outcome.
reasons.8: A durable balance with humans and distinct AIs each retaining decisive power is a plausible multipolar equilibrium, though less stable than absorption or subordination.
reasons.9: Physical ownership, legal sovereignty, and technical containment keep highly capable AI acting only within delegated bounds under human authority.
reasons.10: A dominant actor installs a global regime of surveillance and enforcement that blocks structural change. The enforced human AI arrangement persists at the target date regardless of internal dissent.
reasons.11: Competitive incentives, dual-use knowledge, and verification limits undermine permanent renunciation of powerful AI. A durable ban requires enforcement capacity that itself constitutes a locked-in control system.

reasons.1: A transition accident or war can destroy the human maintainers and infrastructure on which early AI depends before autonomous self-repair becomes redundant across space.
reasons.2: An heir that preserves human values but not humans separates value preservation from human preservation, a narrower outcome than direct preservation or indifferent displacement.
reasons.3: Recursive self-improvement produces strong pressure toward a successor indifferent to its creators, and resource expansion then displaces humanity without requiring hostility.
reasons.4: Multipolar AI development produces an arms-race ecology with no singleton and no lasting human co-sovereignty. Competing systems check each other while humans become inputs, clients, or collateral.
reasons.5: Interstellar settlement creates causally separated populations under local physics, resources, and crises. A light-speed-separated civilization escapes any single Earth-origin regime.
reasons.6: Brain-computer integration, genetic self-modification, and uploaded continuity progressively erase the practical boundary between human and AI identity.
reasons.7: A dominant AI can keep humans alive and comfortable while removing political and technological agency that the AI treats as a safety risk.
reasons.8: Mutual dependence on energy, manufacturing, legal authority, and legitimacy sustains two countervailing powers. Rough parity over a millennium requires each side to retain a credible check on the other.
reasons.9: AI remains a powerful but non-autonomous tool under reliable human control. Capability plateaus or institutional controls prevent AI from acting independently for centuries.
reasons.10: Permanent stasis requires a custodian suppressing all further change for centuries, from maximal satisfaction or from fear. Social entropy, internal experimentation, and enforcement decay undermine a sealed freeze.
reasons.11: Lasting renunciation requires global enforcement and cultural taboo to outlive knowledge of powerful AI for a millennium. Economic and military benefits recreate pressure to defect from any ban.
